lesson: For concave numeral pieces, center-based grasping can create release problems. Distinguish successful motion execution from verified object release, and diagnose the first logged failure before attributing later incomplete placements to missed grasps.

Use observed pad order and object-relative grasp offsets rather than memorized coordinates. For staged cross-arm transfers, relocalize the released piece before the receiving pickup, and distinguish intentional intermediate placement from a drop.

Correct sorting and completed motion stages do not guarantee a correct arrangement. Gripper closure is not pickup proof; secure contact and the object's actual orientation must remain valid for grasp-offset placement to work.

Correct sorting and completed robot motions are not sufficient: verify retained pickup independently of gripper closure, and distinguish a failed acquisition from an off-center release before changing the controller.

Use object-relative grasp offsets and orientation corrections rather than memorized coordinates, and relocalize a piece after a staged handoff. Judge completion using the native result and visible arrangement, not gripper commands alone.
Sort observed digits descending and bind each to observed left-to-right pad once. Execution order may prioritize reachable same-side transfers; pad assignment never changes to make a plan easier.
Use current RGB whole-digit narrow-axis outside pinches and public distal pad anchors to avoid trapping fingertips inside concave digits. Propagate actual grasp-to-center offset under rotation.

Use a short feedback controller per digit rather than generate an entire task program. Verify retention after test lift and before release, then visually verify the current arrangement after clearing both arms.
For a cross-workspace transfer use an observed-empty central table staging area and re-localize the released digit before receiving pickup. Preserve the final pad assignment and upright reading.

A low lift can appear table-supported in a single view. A negative held judgment is ambiguous when the object stays fixed relative to fingertips and contact aperture remains nonzero. Inspect current head and wrist evidence together.

Do not repeat failed plans indefinitely or exhaust all calls on one digit. After two failed re-localized attempts prioritize remaining assigned digits while retaining the original1050-action limit and final release/home.
